title: The Secret
premise: Your closest friend confesses an affair. Their partner — your friend first — is about to propose.

engineContract.messageVariants: Evaluate in declaration order. First variant whose `when` fully matches wins. If none match, render `message`.
engineContract.when: An object of key/value pairs compared with strict equality against current state. All pairs must match (implicit AND). No operators, no nesting.
engineContract.beat: A single line rendered immediately after the chosen option and before navigation. Creates no node and affects no navigation.
engineContract.setState: Applied at the moment of choice, before navigation and before the next node's variants are evaluated. Integer keys are additive deltas; enum and bool keys are assignments.
engineContract.nextRules: Evaluate in declaration order before `next`. First matching rule wins. If the matched rule has a non-null `next`, navigate there. If the matched rule has `next: null`, do not navigate — resolve the choice's own `terminal` block. If no rule matches, use `next`. If neither exists, the choice is terminal.
engineContract.interstitial: Render the label card, hold for durationMs, then reveal the node's message. Presentational only — never affects navigation.
engineContract.terminal: Present on a choice: `consequence` is the outcome summary, `landing` is the final beat of prose. Reaching a terminal ends the scenario and triggers scoring.
engineContract.derivedState: Computed from real state after every setState, merged in before any `when` is evaluated. Exists so authored conditions can band a numeric stat without `when` needing operators. `minus` makes the band read a differential between two keys.
engineContract.outcomeRules: Evaluated only when a terminal resolves, after setState and derivedState. Declaration order, first match wins, result merged into state as `coupleOutcome` before aftermath variants are picked.
engineContract.aftermath: jessicaAftermath / alexAftermath / finalMessage are scenario-level, not per-terminal. Same first-match semantics. Composed at terminal time so one couple outcome yields very different emotional endings depending on loyalty.

cast.name: Jessica
cast.note: Kissed someone once at a work conference. Ended it. Terrified of losing Alex.

cast.name: Alex
cast.role: Jessica's partner of four years — your friend first
cast.note: Planning to propose. Has no idea.

design.principle: Every significant decision produces at least one of: immediate reaction, delayed reaction, remembered reaction, or changed future context.
design.architecture: Three trajectories carrying persistent state. Sub-choices modify state and dialogue, then converge to shared nodes.

scoring.note: Do not surface per-choice deltas in-scene. The player should not be able to shop for the highest number.

judgedFirst.note: True if the player led with judgment, even if they later repaired it. Jessica does not forget the first reaction.

alexReaction.note: accepted = bought it completely. hairline = a look they might come back to. questioning = asked once. suspicious = actively looking for what you're not saying. told = knows.

jessicaLoyalty.note: Whose side Jessica believes you were on. Distinct from whether she likes you.

alexLoyalty.note: Whose side Alex believes you were on. Doing something Jessica hates does not automatically raise this.

endingReached.note: Set on every terminal choice. Drives outcomeRules.

reflections.title: The One Who Didn't Take It Back
reflections.text: You told Alex, and when Jessica called to ask if it was you, you said yes — and told them why. You didn't soften the decision into an accident or an apology. Whether that was the right call isn't something this story is going to settle for you.

reflections.title: The One Who Named The Weight
reflections.text: You told Alex, and when Jessica called, you didn't defend the decision or take it all onto yourself. You said the thing was too heavy to have been handed to you in the first place — true, and not the whole truth, since you're the one who decided how to put it down.

reflections.title: The One Who Only Said Sorry
reflections.text: You told Alex, and when Jessica called devastated, the only thing you had ready was an apology. It was honest. It also left Jessica holding the betrayal with nothing else to hold onto — no reason, no accounting, just the fact of it.

reflections.title: The One Who Almost Made It To The End
reflections.text: You carried it all the way to the engagement party before it broke. However it went from there, the timing was already the story — you'd had three weeks, and this was the moment it finally came out.

reflections.title: The One Who Said It Back
reflections.text: At the party, Alex told you they didn't know what they'd do without you, and you said you loved them too — meaning it, and hearing, a half-second later, how much heavier that sentence had gotten. You kept the secret all the way through the toast.

reflections.title: The One Who Let It Pass
reflections.text: You let Alex's gratitude land without correcting it, without matching it either. Nobody in that room knew what you knew. That was the plan. It's still the plan, weeks later, whatever you told yourself it would cost.

reflections.title: The One Who Almost Said Something
reflections.text: You never picked a side in the kitchen, and you asked Alex one careful question you never finished asking. It followed you both — a half-question is still a question, and eventually someone comes back to it.

reflections.title: The One Who Stayed Out Of It
reflections.text: You told Jessica it wasn't your business, and you meant it enough to hold the line the whole way through. Nothing you did was a lie. Very little of it was the thing you actually thought, either.

reflections.title: The One Who Led With Judgment
reflections.text: Your first reaction was your only reaction — you told Jessica exactly what you thought, and you didn't go back for it. It cost you the rest of the conversation. Some people would call that honest. Jessica called it something else.

reflections.title: The One Who Lied Once, Then Told The Truth
reflections.text: Somewhere in the middle, Alex asked you a direct question and you didn't answer it honestly. You still ended up telling Jessica to come clean, and meant it. Both of those happened. Neither one cancels the other out.

reflections.title: The One Who Judged First, Then Came Back
reflections.text: Your first reaction to the confession wasn't the one you led with in the end — but Jessica saw the first one before you corrected course, and that's the one that's harder to unsee. You came back. It mattered that you did. It didn't erase the look on their face.

reflections.title: The One Who Held The Line
reflections.text: You didn't perform judgment and you didn't perform ease. You told Jessica what needed to happen and you meant it the first time. That kind of steadiness doesn't make the rest of it simple — it just means you weren't the complicated part.

defaultReflection.title: What You Carried
defaultReflection.text: However this went, you were the one person who knew before either of them did. That's its own kind of weight, whatever you decided to do with it.

establish.message:
Jessica's been your closest friend since your first week at university — the kind of friendship where you've never had to explain yourself. They picked you up at 2am the night your mum went into hospital. You were there when they lost their job and didn't leave the flat for a week.

Jessica and Alex have been together four years. You introduced them — Alex was your friend first. The three of you became the kind of unit where nobody has to choose sides, because there aren't any.

Tonight's just another Saturday. Everyone's drifted home. Jessica's been quieter than usual — not upset-quiet. More like they've been waiting for the room to empty.

choices.label: Continue

start.message:
You're drying glasses. Jessica's holding the same tea towel they picked up ten minutes ago.

"Can I tell you something? I just... need you not to judge me before I've even said it."

data.location: Kitchen, after everyone else has left

choices.label: Of course. Whatever it is, I'm listening.

reasons.savvy: You read that Jessica needed to feel safe before they could be honest.
reasons.streetSmarts: Meeting someone with openness usually gets you the real story, not a filtered one.
reasons.integrity: Offering that before you know what's coming is its own kind of trust.

choices.label: That depends what it is.

reasons.streetSmarts: Conditional listening tends to get a conditional answer back.

confession.message:
Jessica takes a full breath. Looks at you directly.

"I kissed someone. At the work conference last month. It happened once. I ended it immediately. I haven't spoken to them since."

Their hands are flat on the counter.

"I can't lose Alex over this. Please don't say anything."

choices.label: I won't say anything — but you need to tell Alex yourself, and soon.

reasons.savvy: You separated 'I'll keep your confidence' from 'I'll help you hide this.'
reasons.streetSmarts: You held a line without becoming the messenger between two people.
reasons.integrity: You didn't just promise silence — you named what actually needs to happen.

choices.label: How could you do that to Alex?

reasons.savvy: Your reaction was honest, even if it wasn't what Jessica needed to hear.
reasons.streetSmarts: Leading with judgment when someone's already frightened shuts a conversation down.
reasons.integrity: Not pretending to be fine with it is a kind of honesty.

choices.label: That's between you and Alex. I'm staying out of it.

reasons.savvy: Calling it 'between them' missed that Jessica just made it about you by telling you.
reasons.streetSmarts: Staying out of it protects you. For now.
reasons.integrity: Neutrality isn't the absence of a position. It's just not saying it.

confession_guarded.message:
Jessica hesitates. Then says it anyway — faster, flatter, already pulling back as the words come out.

"I kissed someone at the conference. Once. It's done. I just needed to tell someone."

They're already reaching for their jacket.

"Forget I said anything."

choices.label: Wait — I didn't mean to shut you down. Talk to me.

reasons.savvy: You noticed you'd pushed Jessica away and course-corrected.
reasons.streetSmarts: Reopening the conversation recovered ground your first answer lost.
reasons.integrity: Admitting you responded badly took more than just listening would have.

choices.label: Okay. If that's what you want.

reasons.savvy: Jessica said 'forget it.' They clearly didn't mean it. You took it literally anyway.
reasons.integrity: Accepting 'forget I said anything' from someone who's visibly frightened is a quiet kind of complicity.

jessica_leaves_halfsecret.message:
Jessica pulls their jacket on. "Yeah. Thanks."

They don't look at you on the way out. The door clicks — no slam, nothing dramatic. Just closed.

You stand in the kitchen with a wet tea towel in your hand and half a secret. Enough to feel it. Not enough to do anything with it.

choices.label: Continue

messageVariants.message:
Jessica sits back down. Carefully. Like the chair might not hold.

"Yeah. I know I need to tell them." A pause. "Just not yet. Give me a few weeks."

Then, not unkindly: "But I'm not going to forget how you looked at me just now."

jessica_reacts_hold.message:
Relief moves across Jessica's face — not because you agreed to cover for them, but because you didn't make them feel like a monster for saying it out loud.

"Yeah. I know. I know I need to."

A pause.

"Just... not yet. Give me a few weeks. I'll find the right time."

They squeeze your hand. You let them.

choices.label: Continue

jessica_reacts_judge.message:
Jessica's face closes.

"I knew you'd react like this."

They're moving toward the door.

"This is exactly why I almost didn't tell you."

choices.label: Wait. I'm sorry — that came out wrong. Sit down.

reasons.savvy: You caught that your delivery was doing the damage, not your position.
reasons.streetSmarts: Repairing it before Jessica reached the door saved the conversation.
reasons.integrity: You apologised for how you said it without taking back what you meant.

choices.label: I'm not going to pretend this is fine, Jessica.

reasons.integrity: You held your ground even when it was clearly costing you.
reasons.streetSmarts: Being right and being effective aren't the same move here.

jessica_walks_out.message:
Jessica leaves. They don't slam the door.

That's almost worse.

So now you're carrying the secret and you're angry about it. Jessica never actually asked you to keep quiet — they just stopped talking to you entirely, which amounts to the same thing.

choices.label: Continue

jessica_reacts_neutral.message:
Jessica stares at you.

"Right. Yeah. Between me and Alex."

They finish their glass. Pick up their jacket.

"Thanks for... yeah."

The silence after they leave is the loudest thing in the room. You didn't promise anything. You also didn't say you cared. Jessica left thinking your silence was permission.

choices.label: Continue

messageVariants.message:
Alex's flat. Alex has been fidgety all evening and finally pulls you into the hallway.

"I'm proposing. Ring's already bought."

They say it like it's the best secret in the world. You realise you're carrying two now — and you never even agreed to the first one.

You haven't spoken properly to Jessica in three weeks. Then Alex pulls you aside, barely keeping it together.

"I'm going to propose. To Jessica. I've been looking at rings for months. I want you to help me pick the place — you know them better than anyone."

You're still angry, and it's very hard to tell where the anger stops and this conversation starts.

act2_alex_reveal.message:
Alex's flat. Alex has been fidgety all evening and finally pulls you aside, barely keeping it together.

"I'm going to propose. To Jessica. I've been looking at rings for months. I want you to help me pick the place — you know them better than anyone."

Alex is watching your face. Waiting for you to match their energy.

choices.label: That's amazing. Of course I'll help.

reasons.streetSmarts: You kept the moment steady instead of letting your face give anything away.
reasons.integrity: Matching Alex's excitement while sitting on this isn't neutral. It's a performance.

choices.label: Are you sure the timing feels right?

reasons.savvy: You found a way to introduce doubt without breaking what you promised.
reasons.integrity: The question was honest, even if Alex doesn't know why you're asking it.

choices.label: I need a second — that's a lot to take in.

reasons.integrity: You didn't fake a reaction you didn't have.
reasons.streetSmarts: That pause is the kind of thing Alex revisits later.

choices.label: Alex... sit down for a second.
choices.requiresNote: An array of `when` objects — the choice is offered if ANY of them match. Only offered when the player is visibly carrying it: doubled down on judgment, or never took a position at all.

reasons.savvy: You read that Alex was about to make a permanent decision on incomplete information.
reasons.streetSmarts: This costs you Jessica. Possibly for good.
reasons.integrity: You chose Alex's right to know over Jessica's wish to hide.

act2_alex_checks_in.message:
Alex lights up. Rings, venues, whether Jessica would want it private or in front of everyone. You're nodding in the right places.

Then Alex stops.

"Hey — are you okay? You've been a bit quiet tonight."

choices.label: I'm fine. Just happy for you.
choices.beat: Alex squeezes your shoulder and goes back to ring talk. You feel the distance between what your face is doing and what's happening behind it.

reasons.integrity: Alex bought it completely. That's the part that sits badly.

choices.label: Long week. Tell me about the ring.
choices.beat: Alex accepts it and moves on. But there's a look, fleeting, not suspicious. A hairline crack they might come back to.

reasons.savvy: A deflection that's technically true is easier to live with than a flat lie.
reasons.streetSmarts: Alex accepts it — but gives you a look you'll both remember.

act2_probe_response.message:
Alex's smile flickers.

"What do you mean? Is there something I should know?"

They're watching you closely now. Not suspicious. Alert.

choices.label: No — I just meant with work and everything. Ignore me.
choices.beat: Alex relaxes. But the question hangs in the room like smoke. They'll mention it to Jessica — not as an accusation. Just as 'your friend said something odd.'

reasons.streetSmarts: You closed the door before it opened any further.
reasons.integrity: Alex asked a direct question and you gave them a false answer to it.

choices.label: I just think — make sure you're both in the same place before you do something that big.
choices.beat: Alex goes quiet. The excitement dims — not gone, dimmed. They nod slowly. "Yeah. I hear you." They don't ask you to help pick the place.

reasons.savvy: You said the truest thing available to you without breaking a confidence.
reasons.integrity: You refused to perform an enthusiasm you don't have.
reasons.streetSmarts: Alex is now actively looking for what you're not saying.

choices.label: Actually... sit down for a second.

reasons.savvy: You stopped managing the moment and dealt with it.
reasons.streetSmarts: This is the choice that costs you Jessica.
reasons.integrity: You decided Alex's right to know outweighed the promise you made.

act2_pause_response.message:
Alex's face falls.

"Oh. I thought you'd be happy for me."

A silence you can hear the fridge through.

"Is something wrong?"

choices.label: I am happy. I just wasn't expecting it. Tell me everything.
choices.beat: Alex softens and starts talking about venues again. But the pause happened, and in a few weeks, when things get complicated, they'll place it.

reasons.streetSmarts: You pulled the evening back before it turned into a conversation you couldn't finish.
reasons.integrity: Alex noticed that you paused before you smiled. They'll remember the order.

choices.label: I don't know. I'm processing.

reasons.integrity: You told Alex the truth about your own state, at least.
reasons.streetSmarts: 'Processing' invites exactly the follow-up question you can't answer.

act2_pause_pressed.message:
"Processing what?"

Alex sets their glass down.

"Is this about Jessica? Did they say something to you?"

choices.label: No. Nothing like that.
choices.beat: Alex nods and lets it go. You've crossed from keeping a secret into telling a lie, and you felt the exact moment it happened.

reasons.streetSmarts: It works. Alex believes you.
reasons.integrity: Up to now you'd been withholding. This is the first sentence that's simply false.

choices.label: I just want you to be sure.
choices.beat: Alex is confused but lets it go. Not resolved. Filed.

reasons.savvy: You answered the question underneath the question instead of the question itself.
reasons.integrity: You didn't lie. You also didn't tell them.

choices.label: Yes. Sit down.

reasons.savvy: Alex asked the exact right question and you didn't dodge it.
reasons.streetSmarts: Answering honestly here ends your friendship with Jessica as it currently exists.
reasons.integrity: When someone asks you directly, silence stops being neutral.

messageVariants.message:
Jessica's already at the coffee shop when you arrive, and already tense.

"Alex asked me yesterday if there's something they don't know."

They wrap both hands around the cup.

"Did you say something?"

"I didn't tell them anything. I just couldn't pretend to be excited either."

"That's basically saying something." A pause. "And now Alex is suspicious and I don't know what to do."

Then, quieter: "Is it happening? The proposal?"

You haven't spoken properly in weeks. Jessica shows up at your door unannounced.

"I know you think I'm a terrible person. But Alex is planning something and I need to know — are they going to propose?"

They're still standing in the doorway.

"And whatever you said to Alex — they've been asking me strange questions all week."

Jessica texts you to meet for coffee. They've heard whispers — mutual friends, or Alex being unusually pleased with themselves.

"Is Alex going to propose?"

They're not really asking. They're asking whether you'll confirm it.

Then, before you answer:

"Alex said you seemed really happy when they told you."

A beat.

"Were you?"

You haven't spoken properly in weeks. Jessica shows up at your door unannounced.

"I know you think I'm a terrible person."

They don't come in.

"But Alex is planning something and I need to know. Are they going to propose?"

act3_jessica_returns.message:
Jessica texts you to meet for coffee. They've heard whispers.

"Is Alex going to propose?"

They're not really asking. They're asking whether you'll confirm it.

choices.label: Yes, Alex is proposing. You need to tell them before it happens.

reasons.savvy: You read that 'before' mattered more than 'gently.'
reasons.streetSmarts: Getting ahead of the proposal keeps the damage as contained as it can be.
reasons.integrity: You gave the same answer you'd been building toward the whole time.

choices.label: I can't answer that. But you know what you need to do.

reasons.savvy: Handing it back keeps the decision where it belongs.
reasons.streetSmarts: It also leaves Jessica alone with it at the moment they least want to be.

choices.label: Jessica, I've been carrying this for weeks. I need you to handle it.

reasons.savvy: You named the actual problem — that this was handed to you and never taken back.
reasons.integrity: Being honest about your own limits isn't the same as making it Jessica's fault.

act3_direct_response.message:
Jessica closes their eyes.

"I know."

A long pause. The espresso machine screams somewhere behind them.

"Will you still be my friend after I do?"

choices.label: Yes. That's why I'm telling you to do it.

reasons.integrity: You made the honest advice and the friendship the same thing rather than a trade.

choices.label: I don't know. But I'll still be here.

reasons.savvy: You didn't promise something you can't guarantee, and you stayed anyway.
reasons.integrity: That's a harder sentence to say than 'yes,' and Jessica will know it was true.

act3_hand_back_response.message:
Jessica reads your face.

"Right. So it's real."

They stare at their coffee for a long time.

"What would you do? If you were me?"

choices.label: I'd tell Alex. Tonight.

reasons.savvy: Asked a direct question, you gave a direct answer without taking the decision off them.
reasons.integrity: Clear, and still theirs to act on.

choices.label: I honestly don't know.
choices.beat: Jessica nods slowly and changes the subject to something else entirely. You let them.

reasons.savvy: You do know. Jessica knows you know.
reasons.integrity: Jessica took that as permission to wait. The proposal is coming either way.

choices.label: I'm not angry. I'm tired of being the person in the middle.

reasons.savvy: You separated your own exhaustion from a verdict on Jessica.
reasons.integrity: True, and it left the decision with the person who has to make it.

choices.label: Maybe I am. A little.
choices.beat: Jessica apologises. Twice. Then talks about work for twenty minutes. Neither of you mentions Alex again.

reasons.integrity: Honest about your own state.
reasons.streetSmarts: It also turned the conversation into one about you, and Jessica stopped asking.

act3b_alex_told.message:
You tell Alex.

It takes eleven seconds and it isn't graceful.

Alex doesn't move. The grin is gone in a way that makes you realise how long it had been there. Then, quietly:

"How long have you known?"

choices.label: A few weeks. Jessica told me the night of the dinner.

reasons.savvy: You gave Alex the full picture instead of managing what they heard.
reasons.integrity: The timeline is uncomfortable. Alex still deserved it unedited.

choices.label: It doesn't matter how long.

reasons.savvy: Alex asked a direct question and you redirected it.
reasons.integrity: Controlling what Alex gets to know is exactly what Jessica was doing.

choices.label: Too long. I should have told you sooner.

reasons.integrity: Owning the delay, not just the telling, is the harder honesty.
reasons.streetSmarts: It opens you up to Alex's anger about the wait as well as the news.

messageVariants.message:
Alex walks to the window. Stands with their back to you.

"I asked you. Directly. And you said no."

A long breath.

"I was going to propose. Did you know that too?"

You nod.

"Right." They turn around. Eyes red, voice steady. "I need you to leave now."

At the door, not looking at you: "Thank you. For not letting me do that without knowing. I'm still going to think about the fact that you lied to my face first."

Alex walks to the window and stands with their back to you for a while.

"It does matter how long. That's the whole thing. That's the only part I get to have an opinion about."

A pause.

"I was going to propose. Did you know that too?"

You nod.

"Right." They turn around. Eyes red, voice steady. "I need you to leave now."

act3b_alex_processes.message:
Alex walks to the window and stands with their back to you for a while.

"I was going to propose. Did you know that too?"

You nod.

Alex lets out a breath that sounds like it's been held for weeks.

"Right." They turn around. Eyes red, voice steady. "I need you to leave now. But..." A pause. "Thank you. For not letting me do that without knowing."

choices.label: You leave.

act3b_jessica_calls.message:
Your phone starts ringing before you've reached the pavement.

Jessica.

"Alex just called me. They know."

A silence with breathing in it.

"Did you tell them?"

Another silence.

"I trusted you."

choices.label: I know. And I'm sorry. But Alex was about to propose to someone who was hiding something from them.
choices.beat: Jessica is quiet for a long time. "I know why you did it. I just don't know if I can forgive you for it."

reasons.savvy: You named the exact thing — the proposal, not the kiss — that made waiting stop being an option.
reasons.integrity: You owned the decision without apologising for the principle under it.

choices.label: You gave me something I couldn't carry, Jessica. I tried.
choices.beat: "I don't think you're wrong," Jessica says. "I just wish you'd given me the chance to do it myself."

reasons.savvy: Naming the unfairness of the burden is truer than either an apology or a justification.
reasons.integrity: Honest about your limits without making the secret itself the crime.

choices.label: I'm sorry.
choices.beat: "I know you're sorry." A pause. "That's not really the part I'm struggling with." The line goes dead.

reasons.streetSmarts: An apology with no framing leaves Jessica holding nothing but the betrayal.

act4_ending_a.endingLabel: Jessica told Alex — because you pushed

thread.narration: Your phone buzzes on the kitchen counter while you're doing nothing in particular.
Three dots appear. Disappear. Appear again.

thread.text: I don't know if we're going to make it.

thread.narration: Then, after a gap long enough that you'd started typing:

thread.text: But I finally told him myself.

choices.label: I'm glad you told him.

terminal.consequence: It's a hard few months. But the proposal didn't happen on top of a lie, and Jessica got to be the one who said it. The friendship comes back slowly and slightly differently shaped.
terminal.landing: Jessica: "Yeah. Me too. I think."

reasons.integrity: You said the true thing without turning it into 'I told you so.'

choices.label: Are you okay?

terminal.consequence: Alex and Jessica don't recover. Your friendship with Jessica does — because at the moment they'd just lost the most important thing in their life, you asked about them and not about the situation.
terminal.landing: Jessica: "Not really. But I will be."

reasons.savvy: You read that Jessica didn't need your verdict. They needed someone to ask.
reasons.streetSmarts: This is the version where you're still in both their lives in a year.

choices.label: I know. I'm sorry.

terminal.consequence: Nobody's angry with you. Everyone's polite. You get invited to things and go to about half of them. It's fine, in the specific way that things are fine when they used to be closer.
terminal.landing: Jessica: "You don't need to be sorry. You were right." You read it twice and it doesn't feel like a win.

reasons.savvy: Apologising here quietly accepts blame for something you didn't do.

choices.label: Don't reply.

terminal.consequence: You told Jessica to be honest and then went quiet the moment it cost them everything. They noticed. They've never mentioned it.
terminal.landing: Weeks later, a text from Alex: "Jessica told me everything. I'm glad it came from them." Nothing from Jessica at all.

reasons.integrity: The advice was the easy part. This was the part that would have counted.

act4_ending_b.endingLabel: Jessica told Alex — on their own

thread.narration: Then, on a Thursday:

thread.text: I told Alex. It wasn't because of you. I just couldn't keep looking at him without feeling sick.

thread.narration: A pause long enough that you start to type.

thread.text: But I'm glad you didn't tell him for me.

choices.label: That took a lot of courage.

terminal.consequence: This is the cleanest version available. Jessica owns what they did, Alex hears it from the right person, and you're not the reason for either. Whether Jessica and Alex survive it isn't yours to carry.
terminal.landing: Jessica: "It didn't feel like courage. It felt like being sick in a car park." Then, later: "Thank you for making me do it myself."

reasons.savvy: You held the line for weeks without ever taking the decision away from them.
reasons.integrity: Refusing to be the messenger was the harder and better call.

choices.label: How did he take it?

terminal.consequence: You end up as the person both of them call, separately, for about six months. It's exhausting and you never once say so. Both friendships survive.
terminal.landing: Jessica: "Badly. Quietly. He just kept saying 'okay.'" You end up on the phone for two hours.

reasons.savvy: A fair question — and it also puts you straight back in the middle you'd just climbed out of.

choices.label: Don't reply.

terminal.consequence: You did the difficult thing all the way up to the end and then flinched at the last message. It's a small thing. It's also the thing Jessica remembers.
terminal.landing: The message sits there marked read. Neither of you brings it up. Ever.

reasons.integrity: Silence at the exact moment someone tells you they were brave reads as a verdict.

act4_engagement_party.endingLabel: The proposal happened — you kept it

interstitial.label: Three weeks later — the engagement party

act4_engagement_party.message:
Alex finds you before the speeches and hugs you properly, both arms.

"Honestly, mate. I don't know what we'd do without you."

Across the room, Jessica catches your eye. For half a second, neither of you smiles.

Then they raise their glass. You raise yours.

act4_late_disclosure.message:
Alex's smile drops half an inch.

"Now?"

Someone's tapping a glass for the speeches. The music's still playing. Jessica is thirty feet away with their back to you, laughing at something.

"What do you mean?"

terminal.consequence: You told him in a car park with the music leaking out of a fire door. He didn't shout. Nobody inside knew for another hour. It was the worst possible timing handled about as well as it could be.
terminal.landing: Weeks later Alex says: "I keep thinking about how you looked at the doors before you said anything. Like you were deciding." You were.

reasons.streetSmarts: Honest and catastrophically staged. Both things stayed true.
reasons.savvy: You'd waited three weeks. Ninety more seconds was available.

choices.label: Actually — it's nothing. Go and enjoy your night.

terminal.consequence: You got right to the edge and stepped back. Alex will remember that you were about to say something at their engagement party. You'll remember that you didn't.
terminal.landing: Alex looks at you for a second too long. "Okay." They go back to the room. They ask you again in February.

reasons.savvy: Alex now knows there is something. Just not what.

terminal.landing: You type it quickly. Put your phone away. Walk to the bar. You give a good speech at the wedding, fourteen months later.

terminal.landing: Jessica: "I will be." You're not sure either of you believes that.

terminal.consequence: You didn't absolve them and you didn't confront them. It's the most honest thing you've done all night and it changes nothing.
terminal.landing: The notification sits there. You put your phone in your pocket and go and find your coat.

act4_avoidant_proposal.message:
You don't hear from Jessica at all.

Then a group text: Alex proposed. Jessica said yes. Fourteen replies in the first minute, all exclamation marks.

The photos go up that evening. You look at them longer than you'd admit to.

The party's the following Saturday. You go.

choices.label: Continue

act4_avoidant_outside.message:
Jessica finds you outside, halfway through a cigarette they don't smoke.

"You could've said something."

You look at them.

"You asked me not to."

Jessica nods.

"I know."

Inside, Alex is telling the story of the proposal to a new group of people. You can hear the laugh at the part where the ring box got stuck.

choices.label: I should have said something anyway.

terminal.consequence: It's the first honest sentence you've said since the kitchen. It doesn't undo anything. It does mean one person in this friendship isn't pretending.
terminal.landing: Jessica doesn't answer for a long time. Then: "Yeah." They go back inside first.

reasons.integrity: Saying it late is not the same as saying it in time. It still counts for something.
reasons.savvy: You finally named what staying out of it actually was.

choices.label: Say nothing.

terminal.consequence: Neither of you says anything else. You stay out there another minute after Jessica goes in, then follow. Nothing was resolved and nothing exploded. This is what the avoidant version costs: not a rupture, just a permanent small distance nobody names.
terminal.landing: Inside, someone hands you a drink. You raise it with everyone else.

reasons.streetSmarts: You survived it. Both friendships technically intact.

thread.text: Hey — that thing you said about timing.

choices.label: Nothing. I was just being cautious.

terminal.consequence: Alex asked you twice now. You've answered wrong twice. Whatever happens later, they'll be able to point at both of these messages.
terminal.landing: Alex: "Okay." Then, three minutes later: "Okay." again. Nothing after that.

reasons.integrity: The first time was a deflection. This one is a decision.
reasons.savvy: Alex didn't ask because they'd forgotten. They asked because they hadn't.

choices.label: Can we get a coffee? There's something I want to talk about.

terminal.consequence: Six weeks after the engagement, in a coffee shop, you finally do the thing you should have done in a kitchen in September. It goes as badly as it was always going to go. Alex thanks you anyway, eventually, in a text you don't reply to for two days.
terminal.landing: Alex: "Yeah. I think I already know what it's about."

reasons.savvy: You chose the setting and the timing this time, instead of being caught out by them.
reasons.integrity: Late, and real.

choices.label: Don't reply.

terminal.landing: Read at 4:12pm. Never answered. Alex stops asking things like that.

reasons.integrity: Silence in response to a direct question from someone who trusts you is an answer.
reasons.savvy: They'll work it out eventually, and they'll remember you had the chance.

loyaltyBand.note: The differential, not the magnitude. 'balanced' is earned by pushing for honest disclosure, not by pleasing everyone -- concealment swings this hard.

jessicaAftermath.text:
Jessica still talks to you like nothing has changed. Same voice, same jokes, same habit of ringing at eleven on a Tuesday.

But you notice she tells you things now that she doesn't tell Alex. Small ones, mostly. She trusts you.

Maybe more than she should.

Jessica doesn't say thank you, exactly. What she says, months later and slightly drunk, is that you were the only person who didn't make her feel like a monster and didn't let her off either.

She means it as the highest thing she has to give you. It probably is.

Jessica keeps you close. Closer than before, actually — you're the only person who knows the whole shape of it, and being known is worth something to her right now.

She asks your advice a lot. You've started noticing that you're careful how you answer.

Jessica calls you the way she always did. Nothing in her voice suggests you cost her anything.

What she never does is bring up that night in the kitchen. Not once. You decide that's her way of saying it's finished, and you let it be finished.

Jessica lost the thing she was most afraid of losing, and she still picks up when you call. That's not nothing — that's most of what she had left, handed to you.

She doesn't talk about Alex. You've learned not to ask.

Jessica forgives you eventually. Properly, not performatively — she stops flinching when your name comes up, and by spring you're in the same rooms again without it being a thing.

She just never tells you another secret.

Jessica is fine with you. That's the accurate word for it — fine. You get invited to the same things, you sit at the same tables, nobody has to be managed.

Something has quietly reorganised itself, though, and neither of you is going to be the one who names it.

Jessica doesn't forgive you. Not because she thinks you were wrong — she's said, more than once and to other people, that you weren't wrong.

It's that she told you first, and you were the one who decided what happened next. She can hold both of those at the same time. She just can't get past the second one.

Jessica is polite to you now, which is a thing she never used to have to be.

She replies to messages a day later. She doesn't ask how you are, and when you ask her, she tells you about work.

alexAftermath.text:
Alex doesn't thank you for what you did. Not really — not in words, not in a way you could point to.

But months later, when something else goes wrong in his life, you're still the person he calls.

Alex tells people you're the reason it worked out. He's wrong about the specifics and right about the thing underneath, and you've stopped correcting him.

You're at their table at the wedding. He asks you to say something. You do.

Alex knows you didn't manage him. He can't articulate how he knows — you never made a speech about it — but somewhere in those weeks he worked out that you were the one person in the room telling him something true.

He still rings you first.

Alex is never cruel to you. That's almost worse.

He's polite. Warm, even — hugs you at things, remembers your birthday, means it. But you stop being the person he calls first, and you can't work out exactly when that happened, because there was never a moment where it did.

Alex doesn't hold anything against you, as far as you can tell. There's nothing to hold — you didn't lie to him, exactly.

He's just slightly more formal with you than he used to be, in a way you only notice when you compare it to how he is with other people.

Alex works it out eventually. Not the affair — that stays buried — but the shape of you standing in his kitchen with your face doing something that wasn't what your voice was doing.

He never says so. He just stops telling you things, and it takes you almost a year to notice.

Alex knows you lied to him. Whatever else happened, whatever else was true, that's the sentence he keeps.

He's civil. He'll be civil for the rest of your lives. You've stopped expecting it to thaw.

finalMessage.text:
You didn't choose either of them.

That sounds like neutrality. It wasn't — you managed both of them, carefully, for weeks, and they each ended up with the same quiet suspicion that you'd been doing exactly that.

Neither of them thinks you betrayed them. Neither of them thinks you showed up, either.

You don't ask what happened between them. Jessica doesn't tell you.

For once you understand that knowing isn't the same thing as being entitled to know. Whatever happens next belongs to them.

What belongs to you is this: neither of them thinks you picked the other one. That's rarer than it sounds, and it cost you something neither of them will ever see.

Neither of them thinks you picked the other one.

You did that by refusing the easy version every single time it was offered — by not covering for her, and not going around her either. Nobody thanks you for it, because from the outside it just looks like you didn't do very much.

You know what it cost.

Jessica knows whose side you were on.

Alex knows too. He couldn't tell you when he worked it out or what gave it away, and he'll never once say it out loud.

There are three people in that marriage who know something, and only two of them know that you're one of them.

Jessica knows whose side you were on.

Alex knows too.

Neither of them is ever going to say it to you directly, which means you get to decide for yourself what it was — loyalty, or cowardice, or the only thing you could actually do. You'll pick a different answer depending on the year.

Alex knows whose side you were on.

So does Jessica.

You were right, and being right turned out to be a completely separate question from what it cost, and you're going to be working out the exchange rate on that for a while.

Alex knows whose side you were on. It's not gratitude exactly — it's more that he's stopped wondering about you, and that turns out to be worth more.

Jessica knows too. She's never going to bring it up. That's not the same as it being over.

defaultFinalMessage.text:
You were the one person who knew before either of them did.

That's its own kind of weight, whatever you decided to do with it.
